description: Spawn a Node child process that hosts `ts-morph` and communicates with the Go API via a stable IPC channel (JSON over stdio or a local Unix socket). Lifecycle-supervised: crash → restart with backoff; health surfaced via `/health`. Hide all sidecar mechanics behind the Connect-RPC interface.

requirements.description: The Go API must spawn and manage a Node.js child process that hosts ts-morph and handles all TypeScript AST operations. Communication between Go and Node must use a stable IPC channel (JSON-over-stdio or a local Unix domain socket). The sidecar lifecycle must be fully supervised: automatic restart on crash with exponential backoff, health probe endpoint surfaced at /health reflecting sidecar status, and maximum restart budget before escalating to a hard error. All sidecar mechanics (spawn, restart, IPC framing) must be hidden behind the Connect-RPC interface. The sidecar must be shut down cleanly on Go process exit.
requirements.title: Node Sidecar Process with Lifecycle Supervision

validation.notes: Test IPC message framing (length-prefixed JSON) for request and response envelopes
Test exponential backoff timing for restart attempts (delays increase correctly across retries)
Test that exceeding the restart budget returns a typed SIDECAR_UNAVAILABLE error to callers
Test that /health response reflects sidecar status (UP, RESTARTING, FAILED) accurately
Test graceful shutdown sends SIGTERM to sidecar and waits for drain before SIGKILL
TCG-SIDECAR-RESTART: Kill the Node sidecar process mid-test and assert Go API restarts it and subsequent Extract calls succeed
TCG-SIDECAR-HEALTH: Assert /health returns UP when sidecar is running and RESTARTING during restart backoff
TCG-SIDECAR-LIFECYCLE: Run 10 consecutive Extract calls and assert no sidecar process leaks (process count stable)
Assert that no ts-morph code executes in the Go process; all AST operations are in the Node sidecar
Sidecar restart and recovery completes within 10 seconds under backoff; subsequent Extract succeeds within normal SLA
Sidecar crash during an Extract call returns a structured error to the caller rather than hanging indefinitely
Operators can observe sidecar health status via /health without inspecting process tables

title: Node Sidecar With Lifecycle Supervision
